candidates.topic: The Hum — Mysterious Low Frequency Sound Heard Worldwide
candidates.teaser: Thousands of people hear a sound that no recording device can ever capture — and it's slowly driving them mad.
candidates.video_title: A Sound Only Some People Can Hear — And It Never Stops
candidates.video_description: Across the world, a small percentage of people hear a persistent low hum with no identifiable source. No microphone has ever recorded it, yet its victims describe it in identical detail. Science still has no answer.
candidates.script: Some people around the world hear a deep, throbbing hum — all day, every day — that no recording device has ever picked up. It sounds like a diesel engine idling just outside. In Taos, New Mexico, two percent of residents reported it so severely they couldn't sleep for years. Researchers deployed military-grade microphones. They captured nothing. Only certain people hear it, and no two explanations agree. So — is it inside their heads, or is science simply not listening hard enough?

candidates.topic: The Demon Core — Physicist Killed by His Own Experiment Twice
candidates.teaser: The same chunk of plutonium killed two different scientists — in two completely separate accidents.
candidates.video_title: One Piece of Plutonium Killed Two Physicists
candidates.video_description: A single sphere of plutonium at Los Alamos killed physicist Harry Daghlian in 1945 and Louis Slotin in 1946 in near-identical accidents. The core was retired after the second death and later used in a nuclear test. It became known simply as 'the Demon Core.'
candidates.script: In 1945, a physicist accidentally dropped a brick onto a plutonium sphere and was dead within a month — from radiation. Nine months later, a different physicist was running the exact same experiment with that exact same core. His screwdriver slipped. Blue light flashed. He was dead in nine days. Two men, one lump of metal, two identical fatal accidents. The military finally retired it — calling it the Demon Core. Some objects, it seems, have a pattern.

candidates.topic: Linguistic Relativity — Languages With No Word for Time
candidates.teaser: There's a tribe whose language has no word for time — and their brains literally process the world differently because of it.
candidates.video_title: This Language Has No Word for Time — And It Changes Everything
candidates.video_description: The Aymara people of the Andes conceptualize the past as being in front of them and the future behind — the opposite of almost every other culture. Some Amazonian languages have no tense at all. Research shows these speakers don't just talk differently — they think and remember differently too.
candidates.script: There's a language in the Amazon with no past or future tense — only now. The Aymara people of the Andes point forward when talking about the past, and backward when talking about the future, the complete opposite of how you think. Brain scans confirm it's not just speech — their memory and time perception are structurally different. Language doesn't just describe your reality. According to the data, it builds it. What does that mean for what you think you know?

candidates.topic: The Moscow Signal — CIA Discovered USSR Microwave-Beaming the US Embassy for 25 Years
candidates.teaser: The Soviet Union silently beamed microwaves at the US Embassy in Moscow for 25 years — and the CIA kept it secret from the diplomats inside.
candidates.video_title: The USSR Microwaved the US Embassy — For 25 Years
candidates.video_description: From the early 1950s until 1979, the Soviet Union directed a low-level microwave beam at the US Embassy in Moscow. The CIA discovered it but classified the information, leaving embassy staff unaware. A later study found elevated cancer rates among employees — the full truth is still disputed.
candidates.script: Starting in 1953, the Soviet Union aimed a microwave beam directly at the US Embassy in Moscow. The CIA discovered it — and said nothing to the hundreds of people working inside for over two decades. When Ambassador Walter Stoessel finally found out in the 1970s, he was already ill. A classified study later showed embassy staff had significantly elevated cancer rates. The official explanation was 'jamming equipment.' The real reason has never been fully confirmed. What were they actually trying to do?

candidates.topic: The Isles of Scilly War — 335-Year War With Zero Casualties
candidates.teaser: There's a war that lasted 335 years — with zero battles, zero deaths, and was only ended because someone remembered to sign the peace treaty.
candidates.video_title: The 335-Year War Where Nobody Died — Not Once
candidates.video_description: The Netherlands and the Isles of Scilly were technically at war from 1651 to 1986 — 335 years — with no fighting whatsoever. The conflict began during the English Civil War and simply was never formally ended. A Dutch ambassador finally signed a peace treaty in 1986, reportedly joking it must have been a tough period for the Scillonians.
candidates.script: In 1651, the Netherlands declared war on the Isles of Scilly — a tiny British archipelago. Then they forgot about it. No battles were fought. No one died. No treaty was ever signed. The war simply continued, silently, for 335 years. A Dutch historian discovered it in 1985 and wrote to the islands. An ambassador sailed over and signed a peace treaty in 1986. The Scillonian mayor joked the islanders could finally sleep soundly. The longest war in history — and not a single shot was fired.
